title: QiMeng-Xpiler: Transcompiling Tensor Programs for Deep Learning Systems with a Neural-Symbolic Approach
problem: Heterogeneous deep learning systems (GPUs, ASICs, custom accelerators) require developing and maintaining multiple low-level tensor programs for different platforms. Current transcompilation lacks effective automation, resulting in high manual effort or functional incorrectness.
motivation: Automated tensor program transcompilation across diverse DLS enables write-once-run-anywhere for tensor code, reducing development burden and improving productivity.
method: QiMeng-Xpiler converts deep learning tensor programs from one hardware platform to another by having an LLM generate candidate code transformations, then using symbolic program synthesis (automated verification) to check and fix them. An automatic tuning system explores different transformation sequences and parameter settings to optimize performance. The system works with four hardware platforms: Intel DL Boost (VNNI), NVIDIA GPUs (CUDA), AMD MI accelerators (HIP), and Cambricon MLU chips (BANG).
key_novelty: The core idea is pairing LLM code generation (for exploring possible solutions) with symbolic program synthesis (for guaranteeing correctness), enabling practical automated transcompilation across different hardware platforms.
contributions: Neural-symbolic transcompilation framework for tensor programs
LLM-assisted compilation passes with meta-prompt guidance
Hierarchical auto-tuning for parameter and sequence exploration
95% average translation accuracy across 4 diverse DLS platforms
2.0x performance vs. vendor-optimized libraries, 96.0x productivity improvement
limitations: Depends on LLM quality for code generation; may struggle with highly specialized or custom tensor operations not in training data.
